To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the selection process for cognate aa-tRNA on the ribosome is governed by conformational motions of the substrate within the A site.

aminoacyl-tRNAs undergo fast conformational fluctuations within the A site of the ribosomes prior to and after GTP-hydrolysis, and that these motions are important in determining the rate of the next step of protein synthesis.

aminoacyl-tRNAs undergo rapid conformational sampling in the A site of the bacterial ribosome prior to and after GTP binding and hydrolysis, suggesting that the selection mechanism is governed by motions in the A site.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that control the rate and specificity of the peptide elongation cycle.
the physical mechanisms that control the fidelity of gene translation.
the molecular mechanisms that underpin the selection of aminoacyl-transfer RNA (aa-tRNA) on the ribosome, which is a central event in the translation process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the conformational sampling of aa-tRNA is an important aspect of the selection process.
the conformational dynamics of aminoacyl tRNA in the ribosomal A-site are critical for the fidelity of translation.
the ribosome uses conformational sampling of aa-tRNA in the A site to control the rate of GTP hydro-lysis and peptide formation, and thereby the fidelity of gene ex-pression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the conformational sampling of aa-tRNA is the key to the fidelity mechanism.

we have provided a detailed view of the structural dynamics of aa-tRNA in the A site of the ribosom, and that the results are consistent with a model where aa-tRNA undergo fast conformational fluctuations in both the pre- and post-hydrolysis states.
the selection process of the correct aminoacyl-tRNAs for the mRNA codon in the A site of the ribosomes is governed by the conformational sampling of aa-tRNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the selection of cognate aminoacyl tRNA for each mRNA codons is achieved, in part, by the ribosome actively sampling the conformational states of the ternary complex, and that the rate of this sampling is a key factor in the fidelity of gene-expression.
the selection mechanism is a highly dynamic process, involving the rapid sampling of aa-tRNA conformational states within the A site.
the ribosome actively samples conformational space during the selection process.
